subject: Dedicated capacity saturation — NebulaAI impact and follow-up
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria@nebulaai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+infra@nebulaai.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] High error rates on Dedicated pool

Hi Mina,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and timeouts on our dedicated pool in us-west-2 around 08:45 PDT this morning. Throughput dropped ~40% and tail latency spiked — several downstream systems have started to back up.

Attaching a small diagnostic bundle (nebula-diagnostics-aug02.tar.gz) and a few request IDs we observed: req-9f1a, req-9f1b, req-9f1c.

Can you confirm whether this is related to autoscaling or an underlying host issue? We need ETA on mitigation and any recommended short-term routing changes. Our SREs are on standby.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Gomez
Head of Platform, NebulaAI
maria@nebulaai.com

--
Attachment: nebula-diagnostics-aug02.tar.gz (diagnostic logs, 2.4MB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria@nebulaai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [URGENT] High error rates on Dedicated pool

Hi Maria — thanks for the heads up and for the bundle.

Quick note on immediate mitigation we applied while we investigate:
- Enabled cross-region fallback routing for active sessions to our us-east-1 warm pool for new requests (non-disruptive, read-only fallback until you opt out).
- Toggled a temporary prefix-KV caching policy for your tenant to reduce duplicate token work (approx 15% token reduction measured in similar incidents).
- Forced a one-time reassignment of a small set of workloads away from the most-saturated nodes.

We pulled the logs you attached and see a correlated stream of eviction/rebalance events starting ~08:44. Initial hypothesis: autoscaler mis-evaluated a transient CPU spike as sustained pressure and began a rebalancing operation that created a feedback loop for a subset of nodes. Ben and Marissa are joining to provide ops details and a short remediation checklist.

ETA: we expect the fallback routing to bring tail latency back under your SLO within 20–30 minutes. I'll follow up with a more detailed timeline and a proposed permanent fix after we complete the runbook review.

Apologies for the disruption — we know how impactful tail latency is for feature pipelines.

—
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity saturation — initial ops notes

Mina / Marissa — quick notes from the infra side after ingesting Nebula's diagnostics and our telemetry: 

Summary of root cause (short): autoscaler decision loop triggered by a short-lived CPU spike on 4 hosts, combined with a backpressure metric configured at a granularity that amplified transient load into sustained node eviction. During the rebalance, KV cache misses increased and a subset of requests started landing on cold nodes — that increased latency -> more evictions.

Key immediate actions taken (some already applied by Mina):
- Enabled region fallback routing (non-disruptive)
- Temporarily widened our backpressure window to avoid treating short spikes as sustained pressure
- Restarted the autoscaler decision agent for the affected pool, which breaks the feedback loop until we roll the patch

Planned short/medium-term fixes:
1) Patch autoscaler to include a 12s smoothing window for the affected metric (PR ready: autoscale-smoothing-12s).
2) Add an adaptive eviction-safe flag that defers eviction when KV cache miss rate exceeds threshold (runbook diff attached).
3) Backfill a small set of warm nodes in us-west-2 to increase buffer capacity during peak windows.

I'll open a change with ops for the patch rollout in the next 6 hours — targeted non-disruptive rollout with canary. We'll include a rollback plan and a one-hour maintenance window if required.

I'll attach the runbook diff and the ops checklist.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

--
Attachment: runbook-fallback-diff.patch (text)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria@nebulaai.com>, ops+infra@nebulaai.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 17:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity saturation — NebulaAI impact and follow-up

Hi Maria / Nebula SREs —

TL;DR: we implemented short-term fallbacks and a targeted autoscaler patch; outage window was 08:44–09:12 PDT on Aug 2. We are offering a one-time service credit for the impacted window and a joint postmortem call next week. Full summary below.

What happened (timeline):
- 08:44 PDT: transient CPU spike on 4 hosts in your reserved pool (internal event correlated with a third-party data preprocessing job).
- 08:44–08:47: autoscaler misclassified the spike as sustained and began rebalancing (evictions triggered).
- 08:47–09:00: feedback loop — increased cold-cache requests -> higher miss rate -> more evictions -> latency amplification.
- 09:00: we enabled cross-region fallback routing and widened the autoscaler smoothing window to break the loop.
- 09:12: service metrics returned to baseline; we continued monitoring for 48 hours.

Root cause: a combination of autoscaler sensitivity and eviction policy granularity that treated a sub-12s transient as sustained pressure. The autoscaler decision logic lacked a short smoothing window and did not consider concurrent KV cache miss signals.

Permanent fixes we will deliver:
- Deploy autoscaler smoothing (12s) and adaptive eviction-safe flag in the next 72 hours (non-disruptive canary rollout).
- Increase warm-node buffer for your reserved pool during your scheduled heavy windows (configurable).
- Add an automated alert rule that surfaces correlated cache-miss + eviction risk so we can intervene earlier.

Customer remediation and compensation:
- One-time credit for the impacted usage between 08:44–09:12 PDT. Our finance team will follow up with the credit calculation and invoice adjustment.
- We propose a 30-minute postmortem review with your engineering and SRE teams next Tue at 10:00 PDT — let us know if another time works.

What you might want to do on your side:
- If feasible, stagger or throttle non-latency-critical preprocessing jobs during your peak windows while we increase warm capacity.
- Share any additional request IDs or client-side traces that correlate with 08:40–09:15 so we can enrich our postmortem.

I appreciate your patience. Our priority is preventing recurrence and ensuring predictable serving economics for your production workloads.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

--
Attachment: nebula-postmortem-summary.pdf (summary, 480KB)
